proved_step: Lemma (ring-buffer append cost). Let B>=1 and let a deterministic streaming machine receive blocks b_t in {0,1}^{r_t}, with total stored prefix length at most B bits. A state consisting of a B-cell circular array, a write pointer j in {0,...,B-1}, and occupied length q can incorporate a block of r bits, provided q+r<=B, by writing exactly r array cells and updating j and q. In a bit-operation model with binary pointers, this update uses O((r+1) log B) bit operations and O(B+log B) state bits; it does not require shifting the previously stored prefix. Proof: write each incoming bit to the next cell modulo B. Each binary pointer advancement and final pointer/length update costs O(log B) bit operations, so r writes and the metadata updates cost O((r+1) log B). In a word-RAM with word size ceil(log2 B), the update takes O(r+1) word operations. This proves that buffering can remove dependence on the existing prefix length from the append operation, but says nothing about the cost of later ordered decoding or oracle queries.

statement: Lemma (ordered read from a circular prefix). Let B>=1 and let A[0..B-1] be a circular array containing q bits, 0<=q<=B, written consecutively from start position a, with next-write position j=(a+q) mod B. Assume none of these q cells has been overwritten. For every k with 0<=k<=q, the first k bits of the stored sequence can be output in order using O(k+1) word-RAM operations and O(1) words of auxiliary storage, with word size ceil(log2(B+1)). Proof: Set the read cursor c=a=(j-q) mod B. For i=0,...,k-1, output A[c] and replace c by (c+1) mod B. Inductively, before iteration i, c=(a+i) mod B. Since i<k<=q and the q stored positions are consecutive cyclic positions from a, A[c] is the (i+1)st stored bit. Thus the outputs are exactly the first k bits in order. Each iteration performs one read, one output, and one modular cursor advance, each using O(1) word-RAM operations; initialization and the k=0 case also take O(1). The cursor uses O(1) words. This establishes an ordered-read procedure for an unoverwritten circular prefix; it gives no bound on later computation or oracle-query cost.

Lemma (trajectory invariance under time-dependent state recoding). Let a deterministic streaming computation have state sets X_t, initial state x_0, transition maps F_t:X_t×Σ→X_{t+1}, and terminal decoder D:X_T→{0,1}. For each t let π_t:X_t→Y_t be a bijection. Define recoded transitions F'_t(y,a)=π_{t+1}(F_t(π_t^{-1}(y),a)) and decoder D'(y)=D(π_T^{-1}(y)); set y_0=π_0(x_0). Then for every input stream a_0,…,a_{T−1}, the recoded computation has y_t=π_t(x_t) at every time t and returns the same output. Proof: At t=0 this is the definition of y_0. If y_t=π_t(x_t), then F'_t(y_t,a_t)=π_{t+1}(F_t(π_t^{-1}(π_t(x_t)),a_t))=π_{t+1}(F_t(x_t,a_t))=π_{t+1}(x_{t+1}); induction proves the state identity through T. Therefore D'(y_T)=D(π_T^{-1}(π_T(x_T)))=D(x_T). The lemma concerns semantic invariance only: it does not imply that π_t, π_t^{-1}, or F'_t have comparable descriptions or evaluation costs.

statement: Lemma (continuation-distinguishable prefixes require distinct states). Let M be a deterministic one-pass machine for a language L over alphabet Σ, with a fixed initial state, deterministic transition maps, and a terminal decoder. Let P be any finite set of input prefixes such that for every distinct u,v in P there exists a suffix z_{u,v} with exactly one of uz_{u,v}, vz_{u,v} in L. Then the states reached after prefixes in P are pairwise distinct, so M has at least |P| reachable states and requires at least ceil(log2 |P|) bits to encode them. Proof: if distinct u,v reached the same state, processing their common suffix z_{u,v} would follow the same deterministic transitions and produce the same decoded answer. This contradicts that exactly one concatenation is in L. Thus the states are pairwise distinct, and encoding |P| states requires at least ceil(log2 |P|) bits. Scope: this gives a state-space lower bound for a chosen family of distinguishable prefixes, but no per-update time lower bound, including for search-MCSP.

statement: Lemma (minimal deterministic streaming state count via residuals). Let L be any language over alphabet Σ. For each prefix u define its residual R_u={z∈Σ*: uz∈L}. In any deterministic one-pass recognizer for L, prefixes with distinct residuals reach distinct states. Conversely, if L has exactly r distinct residuals among all prefixes, a recognizer with r states exists: its states are residuals, its transition on symbol a maps R_u to R_{ua}, which is well-defined because R_u=R_v implies R_{ua}=R_{va}, and its decoder accepts R_u iff ε∈R_u. Thus the minimum number of states is exactly r (or infinite if infinitely many residuals). Proof: the first direction follows by choosing z in the symmetric difference of R_u,R_v; equal machine states would give equal outputs after z. For the converse, the transition is well-defined since z∈R_{ua} iff az∈R_u, and the decoder is well-defined by ε membership. This characterizes state complexity exactly but gives no update-time lower bound.
